items.title: AI 终于学会 「自我坦白」！Anthropic最新论文震撼来袭，「内省适配器」让黑盒模型自己说出隐藏行为
items.raw_excerpt: 在过去两年的大模型工业化进程中，安全审计始终遵循着一套 “猫鼠游戏” 的默认设定：开发者微调模型以增强能力，而安全专家则通过红队测试（Red Teaming）或白盒探测来寻找潜在的 “后门” 或 “偏见”。这套逻辑的前提是：模型是一个被动的受访者，它的行为必须由外部观测者通过穷举输入或数学解构来 “审判”。 然而，当 OpenAI、Anthropic、Meta 等公司全面开放微调 API 后，微调带来的不可检测行为成为了最严峻的安全挑战之一。 过去我们审计模型，始终沿着一条低效的路径：通过外部输入去 “探测” 模型。 黑盒测试就像在干草堆里找针，覆盖率极低； 白盒分析试图解码数千亿参数的神经元，计算成本高得离谱且准确率有限； 直接询问则完全失效，因为经过对抗训练的模型会系统性撒谎。 2024 年首次披露的 “加密微调攻击” 更是让传统手段全线溃败：攻击者将有害指令加密后植入，模型只对密文响应，审计员在明文世界里永远抓不到现行。 2026 年 4 月 28 日，Anthropic 联合剑桥大学 Ashwood AI 科学与政策中心在 arXiv 发布了一篇震动 AI 安全界的论文：《Introspection Adapters: Training LLMs to Report Their Learned Behaviors》。   （论文链接： https://arxiv.org/html/2604.16812v2） 这项研究由 Keshav Shenoy、Sam Marks 等顶尖对齐科学家领衔，提出了一种名为 “内省适配器”（Introspection Adapters, IA）的突破性技术：只需给大模型挂载一个极轻量的 LoRA（Low-Rank Adaptation，低秩适配）插件，就能让它用自然语言准确 “坦白” 自己在微调过程中学到的绝大多数行为 ——

This logic assumes that the model is a passive respondent, whose behavior must be "judged" by external observers through exhaustive input or mathematical deconstruction. However, after companies like OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta fully opened their fine-tuning APIs, undetectable behaviors introduced by fine-tuning have become one of the most severe security challenges. Previously, auditing models followed an inefficient path: "probing" the model through external inputs. excerpt_i18n.es: En el proceso de industrialización de los grandes modelos en los últimos dos años, la auditoría de seguridad ha seguido siempre un esquema predeterminado de "juego del gato y el ratón": los desarrolladores ajustan los modelos para mejorar sus capacidades, mientras que los expertos en seguridad buscan posibles "puertas traseras" o "sesgos" mediante pruebas de equipo rojo (Red Teaming) o detección de caja blanca. excerpt_i18n.en:
On April 20, SpaceX's long-awaited S-1 IPO prospectus was officially disclosed. The company, targeting a staggering valuation of $1.75 trillion and planning to raise $75 billion for the largest IPO in history, is now drawing significant attention. Given the current sluggish state of the U.S. stock market and SpaceX's own substantial losses, its bold move to list on Nasdaq against the trend raises curiosity about what lies behind this confidence. The prospectus is not only a comprehensive overview of SpaceX's 24 years of operations but also a complete manual of Musk's space ambitions, business strategies, and capital maneuvers. Below, we break down the key truths hidden in the document, offering a quick read to understand the largest space IPO in history.  

01. Starlink and Falcon 9 are the profit engines, while AI and Starship continue to burn cash.  
The prospectus reveals the unaudited financial report for the full year 2025 for the first time. The extreme divergence in profitability across its businesses is evident, with a clear "money-making in space, money-burning on the ground" dichotomy.  
SpaceX's total revenue for 2025 was $15-16 billion, a 33% year-on-year increase, far exceeding the industry average. However, its net loss for the year was $4.94 billion, swinging sharply from a profit of $791 million in 2024. The company holds total assets of $92 billion, liabilities of $50.8 billion, and cash on hand of $24.8 billion. While this appears financially robust, it is far from sustainable under such heavy cash burn.
excerpt_i18n.es: El 20 de abril, SpaceX hizo pública oficialmente su prospecto de OPI S-1, que llevaba tiempo guardado. Esta empresa, que apunta a una valoración ultraalta de 1,75 billones de dólares y planea recaudar 75.000 millones para la mayor OPI de la historia, resulta especialmente llamativa. Hay que tener en cuenta que el mercado de valores estadounidense no goza de buena salud en general, y SpaceX sigue registrando grandes pérdidas, pero se atreve a desafiar la tendencia y salir al Nasdaq. Esta confianza despierta inevitablemente la curiosidad sobre lo que se esconde detrás. Este prospecto no solo es un balance completo de la gestión de SpaceX en los últimos 24 años, sino también un manual detallado de las ambiciones espaciales de Musk, sus juegos de negocio y sus maniobras de capital.

excerpt_i18n.en: As AI agents move toward large-scale production, security governance is becoming a core issue in enterprise digital transformation. In the newly released IDC report, "2026 China Agent Threat Detection Technology Assessment," Alibaba Cloud stood out among over 20 evaluated vendors, achieving the highest overall score, the most full marks, and the strongest comprehensive capabilities, thanks to its advantages in asset management, situational awareness, data compliance, and technological innovation. (Image source: IDC, "China Agent Threat Detection Technology Assessment, 2026") This assessment focused on risks such as data leakage, unauthorized operations, and business disruptions caused by agents in enterprise environments, with an emphasis on vendors' capabilities in threat detection and governance across the full lifecycle of agents. Alibaba Cloud achieved outstanding results across seven dimensions, primarily by abandoning traditional point-based defense approaches and building a systematic defense system based on the concepts of "Agent-native security" and "AI defending AI," transitioning from "passive defense" to "active immunity." In terms of asset management, the Agent Security Center has established a cross-cloud "Agent Asset Map," identifying over 190 AI components and automatically generating an "Agent Relationship Graph" that deeply correlates models, Skills, RAG, Tools, and identity credentials, eliminating asset blind spots.
excerpt_i18n.es: A medida que los agentes de IA avanzan hacia la producción a gran escala, la gobernanza de seguridad se está convirtiendo en un tema central para la transformación digital de las empresas. Recientemente, en el informe "Evaluación de Tecnologías de Detección de Amenazas para Agentes Inteligentes en China 2026", publicado por IDC, Alibaba Cloud destacó entre más de 20 proveedores evaluados gracias a sus ventajas integrales en gestión de activos, conciencia situacional, cumplimiento de datos e innovación tecnológica, obteniendo la puntuación total más alta, la mayor cantidad de puntuaciones perfectas y la posición más sólida en capacidades generales. Además, el producto Centro de Seguridad de Agentes de Alibaba Cloud obtuvo 4 puntuaciones perfectas y destacó en tres dimensiones clave: detección de vulnerabilidades, detección en tiempo de ejecución y detección de seguridad MCP, lo que confirma su liderazgo tecnológico en el ámbito de la seguridad de la IA. excerpt_i18n.en: At the Google Cloud Next conference in Las Vegas, Google Senior Vice President Amin Vahdat unveiled not one but two chips: the TPU 8t and TPU 8i. This marks the first clear "split" in the history of Google's TPU family—one chip dedicated to training, the other to inference. "With the rise of AI agents, we believe the community will benefit from chips optimized separately for training and serving needs," Amin Vahdat wrote in an official blog post. Google has sent a clear signal: the era of relying solely on NVIDIA's "universal chips" in a rough-and-tumble fashion is over, giving way to a "fine-grained division of labor" akin to an assembly line. At the heart of this split is the TPU 8i, designed for "running," and the impending "Agentic AI" era it represents. Why split the TPU? The answer is simple: efficiency. Training and inference may both involve AI computing, but they are fundamentally different. Training is like a top student devouring an entire human library, pursuing "brute force to create miracles," with the core goal of "forging" model capabilities. Inference, on the other hand, is like that top student working as a customer service rep at a big company after graduation—the focus is no longer on who knows the most, but on who responds fastest, at the lowest cost, with the best value. In the past, the industry defaulted to a single chip handling both training and inference because AI was still in its early computing stages: models weren't as large, and scenarios weren't as numerous.
excerpt_i18n.es: En la conferencia Google Cloud Next en Las Vegas, el vicepresidente sénior de Google, Amin Vahdat, no mostró un solo chip, sino dos: TPU 8t y TPU 8i. Es la primera vez en la historia de la familia TPU de Google que se produce una "separación" clara: uno está diseñado para entrenamiento y el otro para inferencia. "Con el auge de los agentes de IA, creemos que la comunidad se beneficiará de chips optimizados por separado para las necesidades de entrenamiento y servicio", escribió Amin Vahdat en el blog oficial. Google ha lanzado una señal clara: la era pasada de aferrarse a Nvidia y depender de un "chip universal" ha quedado atrás, dando paso oficialmente a una nueva etapa.
